Definition: a kneading-trough (in which the dough rises)
BiblicalUsage: The word is a kneading-trough, the bowl the dough rises in, and it appears in the exodus and in the blessing. The people took their dough in troughs on their shoulders when they left Egypt, the frogs came up into the troughs in Pharaoh's house, and the blessing promises that the basket and the store shall be blessed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the trough is a sign of daily bread: God provides the dough and blesses the bowl, and even the plagues reach into the kitchen.
